title: Dissertations and Theses
summary: Bibliographies of dissertations and theses receive a combination of [subject]--Bibliography, [institution]--Dissertations--Bibliography, and Dissertations, Academic--[country]-- Bibliography. Dissertations, Academic is subdivided geographically only by countries or larger units, never below the country level.
validation_rules: For a bibliography of dissertations/theses on a specific topic assign `[subject or name heading]--Bibliography`; omit it if the work is not limited to a specific topic. (H 1570 sec. 1)

For a bibliography limited to a specific institution assign `[institution]--Dissertations--Bibliography` (`610 X0 $a [institution] $x Dissertations $v Bibliography.`); omit it if not limited to an institution. (H 1570 sec. 1)
Assign `Dissertations, Academic--[country]--Bibliography` to bibliographies of dissertations and theses. (H 1570 sec. 1)

Subdivide `Dissertations, Academic` geographically only by names of countries or larger geographic units; never below the country level, even for individual institutions: a list of theses of Harvard University gets `Dissertations, Academic--United States--Bibliography`. (H 1570 sec. 2)

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Bibliographies of dissertations and theses may be general in nature, or limited to a particular subject. They may also list those items accepted by a particular institution or the institutions collectively of a particular geographic area. For classification of bibliographies and catalogs of dissertations and theses, see F 585.

sections.heading: 1. General rule
sections.text:
Assign to a bibliography of dissertations and/or theses the appropriate combination of the following subject headings:

```
6XX X0 $a [subject or name heading] $v Bibliography.
[Omit this heading if the work is not limited to a specific topic.]

610 X0 $a [institution] $x Dissertations $v Bibliography.
[Omit this heading if the work is not limited to a specific institution.]

650 #0 $a Dissertations, Academic $z [country] $v Bibliography.
```

sections.heading: 2. Geographic subdivision
sections.text: When subdividing the heading Dissertations, Academic geographically, do not subdivide below the country level even when dealing with individual institutions. Subdivide only by names of countries or larger geographic units. For example, assign to a list of theses of Harvard University the heading Dissertations, Academic--United States--Bibliography.
